planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Daikagura is a classic Japanese camellia cultivar producing very large, peony-form flowers boldly streaked and mottled in rose-red and white, one of the showiest variegated camellia forms.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade. Daikagura is a centuries-old Japanese camellia cultivar prized for exceptionally large, formal peony-form flowers, densely packed with irregularly waved and twisted petals boldly streaked and mottled in rose-red over a white background, a strikingly variegated pattern unique to each bloom. The dramatic size and coloring make individual flowers a focal point in the winter garden, and the plant's dense, glossy, dark-green evergreen foliage provides year-round structure. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars, it blooms in the cool season, typically midwinter in zone 9, when little else is in flower. Plant in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, which scorches the glossy leaves, and mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to protect the shallow, fibrous root system and maintain the acidic soil camellias require.

common_name: Chandleri Elegans Camellia (Antique Anemone-Form Pink Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Chandleri Elegans is one of the oldest camellia cultivars still in general cultivation, introduced in England around 1831, with large anemone-form rose-pink flowers centered by a dense cluster of small petaloids.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade. Chandleri Elegans, introduced in England around 1831, is one of the oldest camellia cultivars still widely grown, prized for large, anemone-form flowers with a ring of broad, rose-pink outer petals surrounding a dense central cluster of smaller, irregular petaloids, a distinctive form quite different from the neat, layered rows of formal-double camellias. Occasional flowers show attractive white mottling or streaking. Its long cultivation history and reliable performance have kept it a fixture in historic and heritage camellia gardens across the South for nearly two centuries. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars, it flowers in the cool season, typically midwinter in zone 9. Plant in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, and mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to protect the shallow, fibrous root system and maintain the acidic soil camellias require.

common_name: Lady Clare Camellia (Large Semi-Double Rose-Pink Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Lady Clare, also known as Akashigata in Japan, is a classic large semi-double camellia with deep rose-pink flowers and prominent golden stamens, a long-favored Southern garden cultivar.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade. Lady Clare, known in its native Japan as Akashigata, is a classic large semi-double camellia bearing loosely arranged, deep rose-pink petals surrounding a prominent, showy cluster of golden-yellow stamens, a looser and more informal look than fully double camellia forms. Its vigorous, spreading, somewhat weeping growth habit and large flower size have made it a long-standing favorite for Southern gardens and historic camellia collections, often trained as a specimen or espalier to show off its graceful branching. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars, it flowers in the cool season, typically midwinter in zone 9, when little else is in bloom. Plant in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, and mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to protect the shallow, fibrous root system and maintain the acidic soil camellias require.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Tricolor is a classic variegated camellia cultivar with formal double flowers striped and streaked in red, white, and pink, no two blooms exactly alike.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.0-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade. Tricolor is a classic Japanese camellia cultivar bearing formal double flowers with neatly layered petals variably streaked and marbled in red, white, and pink, a variegation pattern that varies noticeably from bloom to bloom and even from year to year on the same plant depending on growing conditions. This unpredictable, ever-changing coloring has made Tricolor a favorite among camellia collectors for generations, since every flush of bloom offers a slightly different show. The dense, glossy, dark-green evergreen foliage provides reliable year-round structure between bloom seasons. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars, it flowers in the cool season, typically midwinter in zone 9. Plant in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, and mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to protect the shallow, fibrous root system and maintain the acidic soil camellias require.
